claim: Under the plain view doctrine, evidence is lawfully discoverable when an officer is in a place where he has a right to be, the incriminating nature of the items is immediately apparent, and—as an additional requirement imposed by North Carolina law beyond federal constitutional mandates—the discovery must be inadvertent.
initial_reasoning: In State v. Tabb, the North Carolina Supreme Court held that the plain‑view doctrine requires the officer to be in a place where he has a right to be and that the incriminating nature of the items is immediately apparent, but it did not impose an additional requirement that the discovery be inadvertent. Thus the citation does not support the claim that inadvertence is an extra North Carolina requirement.
